Unless recovery is considered more-likely-than-not (a probability level of more than 50%), we will record a charge to income tax expense in the form of a valuation allowance for the deferred tax assets that we estimate will not ultimately be recoverable or maintain the valuation allowance recorded in prior periods.

When considering all available evidence, if we determine it is more-likely-than-not we will realize our deferred tax assets, we will reverse some or all of the existing valuation allowance, which would result in a credit to income tax expense and the establishment of an asset in the period of reversal.

sentences.text: We face claims based on IP rights from individuals, companies, investment litigation entities, other non-practicing entities, academic and research institutions, and other parties.

In the past few years, we have faced costly and lengthy lawsuits across multiple jurisdictions selected by non-practicing entities with well-funded third-party investment support, including most notably the VLSI and R2 litigation, which have resulted in significant adverse judgments and settlements.

The OECD is continuing discussions surrounding fundamental changes in allocation of profits among tax jurisdictions in which companies do business, as well as the implementation of a global minimum tax (namely the "Pillar One" and "Pillar Two" proposals).

comparisons.peer_summary: Restructuring and other charges recognized in operating expenses were $1,533 million in fiscal year 2024 and $244 million in fiscal year 2023. The 2024 charges primarily consisted of employee termination costs related to cost reduction activities associated with the VMware Merger, while the 2023 charges were primarily non-recurring charges related to IP litigation.

Intel describes ongoing, increasing claims from non-practicing entities leading to 'significant adverse judgments and settlements' (e.g., VLSI, R2). In contrast, Broadcom's candidate notes that fiscal year 2023 restructuring charges were primarily due to 'non-recurring charges related to IP litigation,' while 2024 charges were driven by VMware merger costs. Intel frames IP litigation as a persistent, worsening threat to operations, whereas Broadcom characterizes its significant IP-related charges as a past, non-recurring event in 2023 that has since receded in 2024.

sentences.text: In the past few years, we have faced costly and lengthy lawsuits across multiple jurisdictions selected by non-practicing entities with well-funded third-party investment support, including most notably the VLSI and R2 litigation, which have resulted in significant adverse judgments and settlements.

For example, in February 2024, R2 Semiconductor, Inc., a non-practicing entity, was able to obtain an injunction and recall order against us and our customers in the Dusseldorf Regional Court in Germany that, if enforced, could have caused significant potential disruption to our and our customers' businesses in Europe.
The fiscal year 2023 charges primarily included non-recurring charges related to IP litigation.
The fiscal year 2024 charges primarily included employee termination costs from cost reduction activities related to the VMware Merger.

comparisons.peer_topic: Other Tax Reform Risks and Monitoring
comparisons.peer_summary: Various tax reforms under consideration in multiple jurisdictions could materially impact the company's tax expense, prompting ongoing monitoring of potential impacts on the global effective tax rate and financial statements.
comparisons.comparison: Intel's disclosure centers on active third-party IP infringement claims and litigation, while Micron's comparable candidate discusses potential impacts from tax reforms (e.g., OECD Pillar Two). Both fall under 'Regulation, Legal & Compliance,' but the subjects—intellectual property enforcement versus tax law changes—are distinct. Intel faces tangible legal disruptions (injunctions, recalls), whereas Micron's risk is financial/operational via tax expense variability. No direct comparison of IP risk profiles is possible.

sentences.text: We have seen an increase in patent assertions and lawsuits initiated by well-funded non-practicing entities, including entities funded by third-party investment firms.

The patent litigation environment has also become more challenging due to the emergence of venues adopting procedural and substantive rules that make them more favorable for patent asserters and courts in which injunctions are available for non-competitors.
Various tax reforms are being considered in multiple jurisdictions that, if enacted, contain provisions that could materially impact our tax expense.
We continue to monitor the potential impact of these various tax reform proposals to our overall global effective tax rate and financial statements.

comparisons.peer_topic: USG export control licensing requirements for specific products and regions
comparisons.peer_summary: Beginning in Q3 FY2023, the USG imposed licensing requirements on exports of A100, H100, and other high-performance AI products to China, Russia, and certain Middle Eastern countries, with new rules effective in Q4 FY2024 covering additional regions like Saudi Arabia and Vietnam. These rules require licenses for shipments of products exceeding specific performance thresholds to these restricted regions or entities linked to Country Group D5.
comparisons.comparison: Intel discusses risks from third-party IP claims and litigation, while NVIDIA's primary regulatory candidate focuses on USG export controls affecting sales to China, Russia, and the Middle East. Both are legal/regulatory risks under 'Regulation, Legal & Compliance,' but they address different domains: IP enforcement vs. trade/export compliance. Intel's risk involves defending against infringement suits; NVIDIA's involves licensing requirements for product shipments. They do not share the same specific topic.

sentences.text: We face claims based on IP rights from individuals, companies, investment litigation entities, other non-practicing entities, academic and research institutions, and other parties.

For example, in February 2024, R2 Semiconductor, Inc., a non-practicing entity, was able to obtain an injunction and recall order against us and our customers in the Dusseldorf Regional Court in Germany that, if enforced, could have caused significant potential disruption to our and our customers' businesses in Europe.

In October 2023, the USG announced new and updated licensing requirements that became effective in our fourth quarter of fiscal year 2024 for exports to China and Country Groups D1, D4, and D5 (including but not limited to Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Vietnam, but excluding Israel) of our products exceeding certain performance thresholds, including A100, A800, H100, H800, L4, L40, L40S and RTX 4090.
On October 23, 2023, the USG informed us the licensing requirements were effective immediately for shipments of our A100, A800, H100, H800, and L40S products.

comparisons.peer_topic: OEM Licensing Negotiations and Transsion Litigation
comparisons.peer_summary: In fiscal 2024, Qualcomm extended or entered into license agreements with several key OEMs and Transsion Holdings Limited, while initiating litigation against Transsion in multiple jurisdictions to enforce IP rights against unlicensed products.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Qualcomm (QCOM) face IP-related legal actions, but with different outcomes and strategies. sentences.text: In the past few years, we have faced costly and lengthy lawsuits across multiple jurisdictions selected by non-practicing entities with well-funded third-party investment support, including most notably the VLSI and R2 litigation, which have resulted in significant adverse judgments and settlements.

comparisons.peer_topic: Derivative instruments hedging policy and status
comparisons.peer_summary: The company uses derivative financial instruments, specifically foreign exchange forward contracts and treasury rate locks, to manage exposure to foreign exchange and interest rate risks for hedging purposes, not for speculation. Outstanding derivatives are recognized at fair value based on Level 2 inputs. As of November 3, 2024, and October 29, 2023, the company had no material foreign exchange forward contracts outstanding. In August 2023, the company settled $5.5 billion in treasury rate lock contracts for a $371 million cumulative gain, with $75 million to be amortized to interest expense through October 2034 upon the issuance of $1.75 billion senior notes, and the remainder amortized for future debt.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom utilize derivative accounting concepts to manage financial exposures resulting from operational decisions, though the specific instruments and nature differ significantly. Intel recognizes a $755 million loss in 2024 due to the change in fair value of liquidated damage provisions, which are classified as non-designated derivatives, triggered by construction delays at Fab 34. In contrast, Broadcom discloses a $371 million cumulative gain from settling treasury rate lock contracts in August 2023, which were also settled derivatives but related to interest rate risk hedging rather than contractual penalty provisions. Both companies recognize gains or losses from these non-designated or settled derivatives in other income/expense or net income, reflecting their impact on earnings from financial risk management activities.

comparisons.peer_summary: Derivative instruments are measured at fair value and recognized as assets or liabilities. The accounting for changes in fair value depends on the designation: non-designated derivatives recognize gains/losses in other non-operating income/expense; cash flow hedges include gains/losses in accumulated other comprehensive income before reclassification to earnings; and fair value hedges recognize changes in both the derivative and hedged items' fair values in earnings. For foreign currency and commodity cash flow or fair value hedges, time value is excluded from effectiveness assessment and recognized in earnings via amortization.
comparisons.comparison: Micron and Intel both disclose accounting policies for derivative instruments, specifically regarding how changes in fair value are recognized when derivatives are not designated as hedges. Intel explicitly states that its liquidated damage provisions qualify as a non-designated derivative, resulting in a $755 million loss recognized in 'Interest and other, net' due to changes in fair value. Micron describes the general policy where gains or losses from changes in fair value for derivatives not designated for hedge accounting are also recognized in 'other non-operating income (expense)'. While Micron provides the general accounting framework and Intel provides specific application to a contractual penalty, both confirm that such non-designated derivative changes flow directly through earnings rather than other comprehensive income.

comparisons.peer_topic: Derivative instruments hedging policy and status
comparisons.peer_summary: The company uses derivative financial instruments, specifically foreign exchange forward contracts and treasury rate locks, to manage exposure to foreign exchange and interest rate risks for hedging purposes, not for speculation. Outstanding derivatives are recognized at fair value based on Level 2 inputs. As of November 3, 2024, and October 29, 2023, the company had no material foreign exchange forward contracts outstanding. In August 2023, the company settled $5.5 billion in treasury rate lock contracts for a $371 million cumulative gain, with $75 million to be amortized to interest expense through October 2034 upon the issuance of $1.75 billion senior notes, and the remainder amortized for future debt.

Broadcom discloses its policy of using foreign exchange forward contracts and treasury rate locks for hedging, noting that treasury rate locks settled in August 2023 resulted in a cumulative gain of $371 million recorded in accumulated other comprehensive income. Unlike Intel, which reports ongoing hedging losses on held investments, Broadcom's disclosure highlights a completed hedging transaction (settlement) with a significant gain, and notes that non-designated forward contracts had immaterial gains/losses.

Outstanding derivatives are recognized as assets or liabilities at their fair values based on Level 2 inputs, as defined in the fair value hierarchy.

For derivative instruments designated as cash flow hedges, the changes in fair value are initially recognized in other comprehensive income, net of tax in the period of change, and are subsequently reclassified and recognized in the same line item as the hedged item when either the hedged transactions affect earnings or it becomes probable that the hedged transactions will not occur.
The cumulative gain was recorded net of tax of $44 million as a component of accumulated other comprehensive income as of October 29, 2023.
